activity.title: Hi Priyanka Salot and Harshil Salot , this has dragged on far too long. I've believed in your products and recommended them to friends, family, and colleagues for years. That's precisely why this experience is so frustrating. Your chairs may be solid, but your after-sales support just sucks with no solution. A paying customer should not have to spend over a month chasing a replacement they've already paid for, receive a completely different story from every support representative, and still have no idea where their order actually is. What is the point of having a customer support team if no one can provide a straight answer or actually resolve the issue? Stop the endless runaround. Take ownership of this, fix what has clearly gone wrong, and have someone who can actually resolve it contact me. From where I'm standing, this stopped being a simple delay a long time ago. And worst is the gaslighting from The Sleep Company itself ...more

At this point my LinkedIn is basically a public complaint box. Turns out some companies only start moving when the conversation leaves the private inbox. Still better than another “5 AI tools that will change your life” post, right? Today’s episode: my one-month circus with The Sleep Company , trying to get the chair mechanism replaced. I initially contacted them, asking if I could exchange my existing chair for a newer model. They said they don't offer exchanges, which was fine. So I asked if I could purchase a replacement chair mechanism instead. The first support representative told me they don't replace chair mechanisms, even though The Sleep Company had already replaced the exact same mechanism under warranty a few years ago. After emailing again, they agreed to send a technician. He visited my home using the correct address, inspected the chair, and confirmed the mechanism needed replacement. I paid for the replacement at the beginning of July after receiving a payment link. I was told it would be delivered within 3 days. Unlike my previous warranty replacement, I never received a tracking ID. A month later, there was still no delivery. When I followed up, I was told the order had been returned due to an address mismatch and that a replacement order had been created. Then things became even more confusing. Support emails suddenly started calling me "Uday." I corrected them, but the confusion continued. I raised around 5 support tickets over the past week. Everyone promised a response within 24–48 hours. None were answered. So I called customer support. 31 July: "Out for delivery." Nothing arrived. 2 August: Again, "Out for delivery." Still nothing 3 August: First, I was told it was out for delivery, then during the same call I was told it had actually been delivered on 1 August. How can something be out for delivery on 2 August if it was supposedly delivered the day before? Finally, the representative checked my details. My customer profile was under "Uday Shetty." The shipment was under Alex Anthraper. The delivery address was simply: 2nd Cross, 5600XX, Bangalore. No apartment number. No house number. Nothing. Apparently my package was delivered somewhere on an entire road. The explanation was that their backend migration caused the issue. Help me understand this If your technician had the correct address and successfully visited my home for the inspection, how did the delivery address suddenly become incomplete? Why was there never any tracking information? Why did I have to keep calling customer support just to find out where my order supposedly was? To the co-founders, Priyanka Salot and Harshil Salot , I've genuinely liked The Sleep Company 's products and have recommended them to friends and family over the years. But good products alone aren't enough if the after-sales support is this inconsistent. I sincerely hope this gets resolved, not just for me, but so future customers don't have to go through the same experience. ...more

#DecadeofSkillBox : On this day, nearly a decade ago, I took the leap of a lifetime and established SkillBox, With my dear partners #AnmolKukreja and #RaviPardhi by my side. We founded this firm with a dream born from years of my savings, sweat, and unyielding passion for independent music in India. I poured my soul into it, envisioning a platform that would revolutionize live ticketing with integrity, structured experiences, and a revival for artists who deserved the spotlight. Little did I know that this creation, built on trust and vision, would become the stage for my deepest heartbreak. In early 2022, fate struck hard. A devastating injury on one of our shows left me paralyzed, immobile, and unconscious for endless hours. In my most vulnerable moment, when I needed support the most, #Anmol turned his back. He blocked me out, seized my vested stock options worth over more than 20 crores of my life's work as of this date, and never assigned them, never filed with the ROC. It was theft, plain and raw, hidden behind silence and denial. Why? Because I dared to speak up. I questioned the nepotism creeping in, the scams hurting artists and vendors, the unethical shortcuts for quick profits that screwed over the very people we were meant to uplift. I had built relationships in this industry with honor, laying a foundation for Skillbox in three phases: live events, low-commission ticketing, and automated artist bookings with digital contracts. It was meant to be a bridge for artists and promoters to thrive ethically. But Anmol craved a fast exit, and in his pursuit, he shattered everything. For three years, I've fought this battle alone in the shadows, six months now in the public eye and the pain cuts deeper each day. The betrayal isn't just financial; it's a wound to the trust I placed in a partner, to the dreams we shared, to the industry I love. And #SandipRanjhan ? His role in this only amplified the deceit, choosing scams over helping the music world grow. Yet, amid the tears and isolation, I hold onto hope. This fight isn't just mine but it's for every entrepreneur who's been silenced, every artist exploited, every voice drowned by greed. So many stay quiet, prioritizing business over ethics, blinding themselves to the rot. But I ask you, my network: Where do you stand? Will you choose money, or will you stand with integrity? This story is my call for accountability. Evil must face consequences, and one day, it will. If you've been through betrayal, if you believe in building with heart over haste, let's connect. Share your stories. Let's rebuild an industry where ethics win and say #Nomore . ...more ...more

🎤 The Harsh Reality of Skillbox Events: A Lesson in How Not to Run Live Shows I rarely post rants, but this one has earned it. SkillBox managed to turn what should have been an unforgettable live experience into a frustrating reminder of how corporate greed can ruin art. From the start, it was clear they only cared about ticket segmentation, not audience experience. The crowd was split into rigid tiers, and if you weren’t in the “right” one, you were left with terrible visibility and inconsistent sound. Even Steven Wilson’s quadrophonic setup, which should have been a technical marvel, fell flat because no one at Skillbox bothered to account for the venue’s ground level and acoustics. The sound was a hit-or-miss experience, literally depending on where you stood. And the final insult? F&B segregation. While the “premium” crowd had multiple options, the “silver” section was left with two choices: momos or donuts. That’s not just bad planning; it’s disrespectful to the people who still paid hard-earned money to be there. Skillbox isn’t just making mistakes. They are actively damaging India’s event ecosystem by prioritizing profit margins over fan experience. Live music should bring people together, not divide them with fences, tiers, and tone-deaf logistics. If you want to charge premium prices, deliver a premium experience. Or don’t call yourself an event organizer. We deserve better. Fans deserve better. The music scene deserves better. ...more

FOUR YEARS. ONE CORPORATE DISPUTE. NOW AN FIR AND AN LOC. The ₹5 crore defamation battle involving LinkedIn and SkillBox has taken a dramatic turn, with FIR No. 209/2026 registered against SkillBox co-founder. The FIR presents written communications concerning existing monetary claims as alleged “extortion.” But ₹6.7 crore claim was formally raised before SkillBox , its board and through legal channels in 2022. How does a documented corporate claim from 2022 become alleged extortion in 2026? The FIR follows ongoing defamation proceedings in which LinkedIn and Bhardwaj are co-defendants. LinkedIn subsequently moved the High Court of Karnataka - India , where an interim stay was granted in connected proceedings. Bhardwaj says he cooperated, appeared before the police and submitted a 135-page documentary response. Yet an LOC resulted in him being stopped at immigration : with its originating request, approval chain and grounds still undisclosed to him. Upon appearing at the station, he says the inquiry appeared dominated by SkillBox ’s narrative before his evidence received equivalent consideration. He is now seeking supervisory and judicial scrutiny of the LOC, Bengaluru jurisdiction, handling of evidence and the role if any of Warner Music Group or other corporate stakeholders. An FIR is an allegation, not a verdict. An LOC is a serious state restraint, not a corporate pressure mechanism. The matter remains sub judice. All allegations are contested.

Research has a way of teaching patience. Some experiments failed, models refused to improve, chapters were rewritten more times than I'd like to admit, and there were moments when progress felt painfully slow. Looking back, those challenges became some of the most valuable learning experiences of my master's journey. 🎓I'm excited to share that I have completed my Master's in Data and Knowledge Engineering at Otto-von-Guericke University Magdeburg . Over the past several months, I've had the opportunity to dive into one of the areas that fascinates me most: the intersection of Artificial Intelligence and legal information retrieval. That journey resulted in my master's thesis 📖 "Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Knowledge Graphs and Embedding-Based Semantic Similarity for Legal Statute Search." This journey has been far more than writing a thesis. It challenged me to explore legal AI, Knowledge Graphs, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), embedding models, and large language models while learning how to approach research systematically. I'm especially proud that this research also contributed to our participation in "COLIEE 2025 (Competition on Legal Information Extraction/Entailment)", and that our work has been published in the COLIEE 2025 Proceedings 📄 . Seeing months of research culminate in both a thesis and a publication is incredibly rewarding. This achievement would not have been possible without the incredible people who supported me throughout this journey. My deepest gratitude goes to my advisor, Sabine Wehnert . Your constant encouragement, patience, constructive feedback, and unwavering belief in me kept me moving forward, even during the most challenging phases of this research. I would also like to sincerely thank Prof. Dr.-Ing. Ernesto William De Luca and Dr. David Broneske for their valuable guidance, feedback, and support, and for taking the time to evaluate my work. Most importantly, thank you to my family. Nothing is possible without unconditional support and belief in me, which gave me the strength to keep pushing forward, even when the journey felt overwhelming. And to my friends, thank you for every conversation, every word of encouragement, every distraction when I needed one, and for always reminding me that there is life beyond deadlines. Looking back, this thesis was not just about developing a RAG framework using Knowledge Graphs; it was about learning perseverance, resilience, and the joy of solving challenging problems. Completing this thesis marks the end of one chapter and the beginning of another. I'm excited to continue exploring the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, Knowledge Graphs, Natural Language Processing, and Legal AI, and I'm looking forward to the opportunities ahead.

Implementing an enterprise AI chatbot involves more than just integrating a large language model (LLM) and connecting it to a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline. While the initial steps may seem straightforward—deploying the LLM, equipping it with the necessary tools, and linking it to your data—the real challenge lies in ensuring effective communication, understanding user intent, and providing accurate, context-aware responses. The nuances of user interactions, data management, and continuous learning play a crucial role in the success of an AI chatbot. It’s essential to consider these factors to truly harness the potential of AI in enterprise settings.

Everyone's talking about AI. And honestly? The demos are impressive. An LLM reads 200 emails, classifies them, sends personalised replies, and wraps up in 2 minutes what used to take a person 3 hours. That's real. That's not hype. But here's what nobody's posting about: What happens when you have 50 of those scripts running across your organisation? Who's watching them? What are they deciding? What happens when one fails — silently — at 2am? A ChatGPT demo is easy to build. Production-grade AI infrastructure is not. The difference between the two is the difference between a cool proof-of-concept and something you can actually trust with your operations, your customers, and your reputation. Most organisations are somewhere in between right now — excited by the possibilities, but quietly anxious about the lack of control. That gap — between demo and production — is the most important problem in enterprise AI right now. And very few people are talking about it. Are you building AI into your workflows? I'd love to know — are you at the demo stage, or have you crossed into production?

You do not have a career problem. You have a clarity problem. There is a difference. A career problem means the market is broken, opportunities do not exist, or your background is holding you back. And when you do not have that answer, everything else gets harder. The resume feels hollow. The interviews feel off. The job search feels like you are throwing things at a wall. We have seen this pattern hundreds of times at Beyond Gurukul. Not with people who are failing. With people who are good. And stuck. On May 9th we are running a session specifically for this. Not to motivate you. Not to give you a five step framework. To help you get one thing: a clearer answer to what you are building and what your actual next move is. For anyone working in content- whether you're in streaming, brand storytelling, or production- pay attention to what's happening in India right now. Last night I watched #Dhurandhar . 3 hours and 34 minutes. No popcorn breaks. Completely absorbed. After my many years in the film industry, I've developed a certain...skepticism when it comes to big-budget productions. The bigger the machine, the harder it is to keep it all intact. This film reminded me in a way why I fell in love with fast paced storytelling in the first place. Director Aditya Dhar hasn't just made a action/spy thriller with quick-cut action sequences (dancing on the edge of gore)..he's crafted an epic that somehow feels both intimate and grand. The fact that he wrote, directed AND produced speaks to a level of creative control we rarely see anymore and that..how you protect a vision. Indian cinema has changed. There's a boldness now. Filmmakers are taking risks we didn't see ten years ago. Not just technically or narratively, but culturally. Pushing what's acceptable to show on screen and that shift matters. A decade ago, this kind of production scale was reserved for Hollywood. Today, Jio Studios and B62 Studios w/ producer Jyoti Deshpande and Co. deliver a movie that stands shoulder to shoulder with anything coming out of the global market. The cinematography by vikash nowlakha is atmospheric and rich. Shashwat Sachdev's score works really well and the performances by actors Ranveer Singh, Akshaye Khanna, Sanjay Dutt are spot on. But here's what really gets me: These filmmakers aren't trying to BE Hollywood anymore. They're creating their own language. Their own scale. Their own stories rooted in history, identity, and cultural complexity. That's the evolution. That's what we should be talking about. For anyone working in content- whether you're in streaming, brand storytelling, or production- pay attention to what's happening in India right now because Indian action cinema has just entered a new era. Ps. Have you seen it? What did you think? /Mikael

World Food India 2025 (WFI) marked the beginning of a new chapter in the friendship between Portugal and India. Rooted in centuries of shared history and mutual respect, this partnership now looks far beyond trade. It is about two nations recognizing in each other a kindred spirit: Portugal, a bridge to Europe, Africa, and Latin America, and India, with its boundless energy and entrepreneurial drive. Together, they stand as companions in shaping a more connected, sustainable, and human future. The possibilities are limitless. At PIBHub - Portugal India Business Hub , our purpose is to turn dialogue into opportunity and partnerships into progress. At WFI 2025, that mission came to life as we proudly led the official Portuguese delegation, showcasing the strength and ambition of our agri-food sector. We built bridges to unlock new markets, and the shared spirit of Portugal and India shone with purpose. WFI 2025 was a showcase with 90+ countries, 2,000+ exhibitors, and 25+ sessions across 100,000 sqm of exhibition and over ₹1 lakh crore (€11.5+ billion) in MoUs signed. Milestones: _ Launch of Coracao Do Vale : A premium Portuguese extra virgin olive oil introduced to the Indian market for the first time, symbolizing the fusion of tradition, quality, and collaboration. Led by Lagar do Vale and LeadsConnect Brand Solutions . _ Two landmark MoUs: One to promote Portuguese agri-food excellence in India, and another to position Portugal with a strategic technology platform for global agribusiness, innovation, and digital collaboration. _ High-level G2G engagement: A pivotal meeting between Shri Chirag Paswan, Minister of Food Processing Industries (India), and Eng. João Moura, Secretary of State for Agriculture (Portugal), laying the groundwork for cooperation in agriculture, technology, and trade. _ Strengthened institutional ties: João R. de Almeida, Ambassador of Portugal to India, and Eng. Altino Álvares , President of PIBhub, reinforcing the strategic commitment. The Success of this mission was only possible thanks to the shared vision of all the delegation members and partners. Our gratitude to Amit Kashyap , Allpanna Venture Advisors . Our special thank you to Ambassador Puneet Roy Kundal . Together, we proved what’s possible when purpose unites people across continents. This momentum is now driving deeper collaboration, investment, and new projects. PIBhub will continue leading this journey, where Portugal and India stand as trusted partners on the global stage.
